prompt: SNES-era 16-bit pixel art sprite concept for a horizontal arcade shoot-'em-up: a single TRENCH EEL enemy of the Iron Tide, a long armored mechanical eel that lunges out of a fortress floor hatch, isolated. At the bottom right a short square steel deck hatch frame with amber hazard lights and a dark open hole. Out of it the eel rears up in a tall S-curve, its body made of a chain of overlapping gunmetal ring-plate segments that shrink toward the hatch, each plate with a steel highlight on the top-left and a darker iron underside, and a thin glowing violet seam running along its belly. At the top the head bends forward to face left: a blunt armored wedge snout with a jagged ridge of steel teeth along the jaw, a narrow slit eye glowing amber, and two small swept-back fin spikes behind the head. Long, sinuous, clearly segmented silhouette. Side view facing left, the whole eel and hatch centered with a generous empty margin on all sides on a perfectly flat solid pure bright green chroma-key background that fills the whole image. Crisp chunky pixel art with a 1-pixel near-black navy outline at the sprite's native pixel scale, flat saturated fills with three-step shading ramps lit from the top-left, bold simple shapes that stay readable at small size, no anti-aliasing, no floor, no water, no scenery, no stars, no cast shadow, no glow bleeding onto the background, no text, no labels.
